created_by: FlameLens data team, with an SI tool
si_use: An SI tool (Claude) chose the files, wrote and ran the scripts that downloaded NASA's DAFT files, copied each bag's averages, mass per particle and diameter cell by cell from NASA's spreadsheets, cut the quoted sentences from the final report and fact sheet, and wrote REPORT.md. It also judged which tests the files describe (three sample bags and one aborted session that PSI's table lacks) and which sentences to quote; those judgements are listed in REPORT.md. Scripts re-read every spreadsheet claim from its cell, checked every quote against two separate text extractions of the report (antiword and LibreOffice), and recomputed NASA's averages from the logged and voiced-down readings. No value was generated or estimated. No person has checked it yet. For the Guide findings the SI tool chose the sentences, and a script cuts each one word for word from the PDF's text and stops if it is not found.
summary: DAFT, the 2005-2006 ISS test of the P-Trak particle counter used by SAME: per sample bag, NASA's mean particle count (P-Trak), mass concentration (DustTrak), mass per particle and particle diameter, each as four NASA sheets state it; the dates and materials of the two cabin-air sessions PSI already holds; and 22 results NASA states in its final report and fact sheet. 70 claims on 6 tests, 4 of them new. Version 2: 1 finding in NASA's words from NASA's ISS Researcher's Guide: Combustion Science (2015), one of the challenge's listed resources.
